title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 107
paragraphs: When Mandane had been married to Cambyses, in the first year Astyages saw another vision. It seemed to him that from the womb of this daughter a vine grew, and this vine overspread the whole of Asia. Having seen this vision and delivered it to the interpreters of dreams, he sent for his daughter, then with child, to come from the land of the Persians. When she had come, he kept watch over her, intending to destroy whatever should be born of her, for the Magian interpreters of dreams had signified to him that the offspring of his daughter would be king in his place. Astyages, then, wishing to guard against this, when Cyrus was born, called Harpagus, a man who was of close kin to him and whom he trusted above all the other Medes, and had made him manager of all his affairs; and to him he said as follows: “By no means neglect, Harpagus, the matter that I shall lay upon you to do, and beware lest you set me aside and, choosing the advantage of others instead, bring yourself afterwards to destruction. Take the child whom Mandane has borne, and carry it to your house and slay it; and afterwards bury it in whatever manner you yourself wish.” To this he answered: “O king, never yet at any past time have you discerned in me an offence against you, and I keep watch over myself also with a view to the time that is to come, that I may commit no error toward you. If, then, it is indeed your pleasure that this should be done, my service at least must be fittingly rendered.”
